question: How many of the 18 crew still missing from the HS Dignity and Wine Trader Black Sea attacks will have their bodies recovered by October 29, 2026?

validation_errors_first_attempt: percentiles must be strictly increasing: p10=0.0 >= p25=0.0
calls.reasoning: Reference class: missing crew of ships sunk or burned in open sea. Usually most are never recovered, and recoveries mostly happen in the first days. As of Oct 19 searches found no reported recoveries. Bulgaria suspended the HS Dignity search on Oct 14; it sank about 17nm offshore, so recovery from the wreck within 10 days is unlikely and only sporadic wash-ups are plausible. Wine Trader stayed afloat and its fire burned through the accommodation block, so missing crew may be aboard. Boarding or salvage could recover several remains at once, which drives the upper tail. Market check: the harness found none on Polymarket or Manifold; I did not check Kalshi or bookmakers.
calls.dossier:
- HS Dignity (Guinea-Bissau flag), 16 crew: 5 rescued, 11 missing. Sank about 17nm off Bulgaria after a drone strike on Oct 13, 2026 (Euronews/Novinite, Oct 13-15).
- Bulgarian authorities ended the HS Dignity search-and-rescue on Oct 14 because of worsening weather (search summary of Bulgarian reporting, Oct 14-15).
- Wine Trader (San Marino flag, empty chemical tanker), 12 crew: 5 rescued, 7 missing. Hit about 13nm SE of Sulina on Oct 15. The drone struck the superstructure and the fire burned through the accommodation block and wheelhouse (shipuniverse, gCaptain, Oct 15). Some early reports said 8 missing.
- Wine Trader appears not to have sunk. No report found on whether the fire was put out, the ship towed, or anyone boarded it. Missing crew may be aboard in the burned accommodation.
- As of Oct 16 (question background) no bodies of the 18 had been recovered. Searches on Oct 19 found no reports of recoveries.
- Reuters/Aftonbladet (Oct 19) still counted 23 killed or missing across the attacks, and one outlet described the 11 HS Dignity crew as 'killed'. No bodies reported.
- Weather: rough seas were hampering the search through mid-October.
- Status quo outcome: 0 recovered.
- Base rates: open-sea sinkings usually leave most missing crew unrecovered, with recoveries mostly in the first days. For fires on vessels that stay afloat, remains are often found once the ship is boarded or salvaged (class: burned-but-floating ships).
- Resolves off credible reporting of bodies attributed to these two vessels' missing crew, not off presumed deaths.
- Event window: Oct 16 -> Oct 29, 2026 23:59 UTC. As of Oct 19 about 25% has elapsed.
- Searched but not found: Wine Trader salvage/boarding status, any wash-up reports on the Bulgarian or Romanian coast, any plan to dive on the HS Dignity wreck, any prediction market.
calls.reference_class: Missing crew in open-sea ship sinkings/fires (e.g. Black Sea attack losses, cargo sinkings): fraction of bodies recovered within ~2 weeks

calls.reasoning: Base rate from the comparable Oct 6 Alfa Watan sinking off Bulgaria: 0 of 10 missing recovered after search ended within a day. HS Dignity search was called off Oct 14 with no remains found; the ship sank fast, so bodies are likely in the wreck with no diver plans reported. Wine Trader stayed afloat and rescuers boarded it Oct 16 with no bodies reported, so the missing likely went into a stormy sea. Through Oct 19 there are no recoveries in English, Romanian or Bulgarian sources. Upside paths: bodies washing ashore near the Danube delta or Bulgarian coast in the coming 10 days, a later inspection of the Wine Trader, or wreck diving. No human market found (Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi, bookmakers).
calls.dossier:
- HS Dignity sank ~17 nm east of Shabla/Krapets, Bulgaria, after a drone strike at ~01:20 on Oct 13, 2026. 5 rescued, 11 missing (maritime.bg, armymedia.bg, Oct 13-14).
- Bulgaria ended the HS Dignity search Oct 14 at 15:00 because of NE winds up to 72 km/h and 5 m waves. Neither survivors nor remains of the vessel were found. A navigational warning asked passing ships to report objects in the water (trafficnews.bg, Oct 14; maritime.bg, Oct 14: no active SAR as of 08:00 Wednesday). No diver or wreck-salvage plans were found in any report.
- An HS Dignity survivor (ruse.news, Oct 19) said the ship sank extremely fast and dragged people down with it.
- Wine Trader (San Marino flag, empty chemical tanker, 118 m long) was hit by drones Oct 15 ~13 nm SE of Sulina; the first drone hit the accommodation area. Fire was extinguished and the ship was anchored near the Danube channel entrance. 5 rescued and taken to Constanta; 7 missing (gCaptain, shipuniverse, Riviera, Oct 15).
- Wine Trader SAR was suspended overnight Oct 15 for weather and resumed Oct 16 with a Black Hawk and the FIFI MAI 0101 vessel; 4 IGSU rescuers were landed on the ship by helicopter (ziuaconstanta, jurnaluldearges, Oct 16). No body found aboard was reported.
- Aftonbladet/Reuters (Oct 19) still describes the HS Dignity 11 and Wine Trader 7 as killed or missing, with no recoveries mentioned.
- Comparable case: Alfa Watan sank Oct 6, ~70 nm east of Byala, Bulgaria. 10 missing; only a capsized boat, life jackets and equipment were found; search called off Oct 7 and not resumed (sofiaglobe, Oct 7). No bodies were reported as of mid-October.
- Status quo: 0 of 18 bodies recovered as of Oct 19.
- Rates: for drone-sunk ships off Bulgaria in Oct 2026, 0/10 recovered within ~2 weeks (Alfa Watan). For the Wine Trader (still afloat, already boarded), no on-board recovery has been reported within 4 days.
- Possible recovery routes: bodies drifting ashore (Wine Trader was 13 nm off the Danube delta coast; HS Dignity 17 nm off Bulgarian coast), a port inspection of the Wine Trader, or diving on the HS Dignity wreck (none announced).
- Resolution: credible-source reports of bodies attributed to these two vessels' missing crew; presumed-dead does not count; ambiguity resolves to the lowest firmly established number.
- Event window: incidents Oct 13/15 -> 23:59 UTC Oct 29, 2026. As of Oct 19, roughly 10 days remain.
- Searched but not found: any body recovery for either vessel, Wine Trader towing or port-inspection news after Oct 16, HS Dignity wreck depth or diving plans, any prediction market.
calls.reference_class: Missing crew from merchant ships sunk or burned by drone strikes in the western Black Sea, 2026 (Alfa Watan Oct 6: 0/10 recovered after ~2 weeks)

calls.reasoning: Reference class: missing crew of ships sunk by drone/missile strikes in this Black Sea campaign. Alfa Watan (Oct 6): 0 of 10 bodies recovered ~13 days later, search called off within a day. HS Dignity sank ~15-17 nm off Krapets and Bulgaria abandoned the search, so its 11 probably stay at 0 unless bodies wash ashore. Wine Trader stayed afloat and was towed to port; the drone hit the crew living quarters and Romanian teams searched the ship, so some of its 7 could be found aboard, which is the main upside. No bodies were reported as of Oct 19 (Aftonbladet/Reuters still lists all 7 as missing). Market check: none found on Polymarket, Manifold or Kalshi, and no bookmaker line.
calls.dossier:
- HS Dignity (Guinea-Bissau flag) sank after a drone strike ~15-17 nm east of Krapets, Bulgaria, on Oct 13, 2026; 11 missing (BTA reported 6 rescued and 10 missing; the question fixes the cohort at 11) [CNN Oct 13; BTA].
- BTA: Bulgaria officially ended the HS Dignity search at 3 p.m. after the weather worsened (N-NE gusts up to 72 km/h). No diving or recovery plans were mentioned [bta.bg, ~Oct 14-16].
- Alfa Watan (Togo flag, sank Oct 6 off Bulgaria): search called off Oct 7. As of mid/late Oct, no bodies found for any of the 10 crew, only a capsized boat, life jackets and equipment [sofiaglobe Oct 7; npasyria; Enab Baladi].
- Wine Trader (San Marino flag) was hit by drones on Oct 15, ~13 nm SE of Sulina. The first drone struck the crew living quarters (accommodation block) around 04:00, followed by two more drones. 12 crew: 5 rescued, 7 missing [marinelink; gCaptain; Al Jazeera Oct 15].
- Baird Maritime: the Wine Trader stayed afloat and was towed to port. A Romanian interior ministry spokesperson said teams 'returned today to search the ship and continue the mission to identify the rest of the crew' (Oct 16). One report says the crew put out the fire.
- Earlier reports mention overturned lifeboats and empty lifejackets found in this campaign's attacks [ibtimes].
- Aftonbladet/Reuters tally (Oct 19): 23 dead or missing across six attacks. The Wine Trader's 7 are still listed as missing, and no bodies had been reported for any of the 18 as of Oct 19.
- Status quo: 0 recovered.
- Resolves off credible media/authority reports of bodies attributed to these two ships' missing crew, counted as of Oct 29 23:59 UTC. Crew presumed dead without a body do not count.
- Event window: incidents Oct 13/15 -> Oct 29, 2026 23:59 UTC. As of Oct 19, about 10 days remain.
- Searched but not found: Wine Trader's current port, whether forensics have searched the burned accommodation, HS Dignity wreck depth, any diver/salvage plans, any shore wash-ups in Bulgaria/Romania. No market on Polymarket, Manifold or Kalshi.
calls.reference_class: Missing crew from merchant ships sunk or burned by drone strikes in the Black Sea, 2023-2026 (esp. Alfa Watan, Oct 2026), bodies recovered within ~2 weeks

calls.reasoning: Status quo is 0: no bodies reported for any of the 18 as of Oct 19. HS Dignity sank fast ~17nm off Bulgaria, search ended Oct 14, no dive plans; comparable Alfa Watan (Oct 6) yielded 0/10 bodies. Wine Trader stayed afloat with the crew quarters struck and burned; Romanian teams boarded and say they are still working to 'identify the rest of the crew', so a cluster of on-board remains is the main upside, discounted because none has been reported after 4 days and DNA identification may run past Oct 29. Isolated wash-ups near the Danube delta or the Bulgarian coast add a small tail. No human market found (Polymarket, Manifold and Kalshi checked by the runs; harness found none).
calls.reconciliation: The runs agree on the facts: no bodies by Oct 19, HS Dignity search ended Oct 14, Alfa Watan 0/10. The dispute is over the Wine Trader. Run 2 says rescuers boarded it Oct 16 and reported no body. Run 3 says it was towed to port and teams are still searching it and working to identify crew. These are compatible but unresolved: there is no evidence of a full forensic search of the burned crew quarters, and none of a recovery. With no web access I could not check further. I give moderate weight to remains being aboard and discount it for the lack of reports after 4 days and the likely delay in attribution, which puts P(0) at about 0.72 with a clustered right tail. The 90th percentile sits between Run 2 and Run 3 because of that reading of the evidence, not by averaging.

disagreements.claim: Wine Trader was searched on board with no bodies found
disagreements.verdict: Unsettled. Boarding on Oct 16 is reported, but no thorough search of the burned crew quarters and no finding either way; the uncertainty is carried in the upper tail.

disagreements.claim: Wine Trader towed to port, where an inspection is possible
disagreements.verdict: Only Run 3 reports this (Baird Maritime); Run 2 has it anchored near Sulina. It cannot be checked, but either way an inspection is possible.

disagreements.claim: Wine Trader's missing crew went into the sea rather than staying aboard
disagreements.verdict: The drone hit the crew quarters, which favours some being aboard; no finds after 4 days favours the sea. Weighed as roughly 28% chance of at least one recovery.

disagreements.claim: HS Dignity recoveries are near zero
disagreements.verdict: Agreed by all runs: search over, no dive plans, Alfa Watan precedent.
